Want to learn more about Orthodoxy?

You do not need to learn everything at once. If something you experienced today has made you curious, here are a few places to begin. Every one of them is the Archdiocese's or the parish's own — nothing here sends you off to a stranger's opinion of Orthodoxy.

Show the reading list
The Orthodox Christian faith
A basic introduction to Orthodox Christianity, from the Archdiocese.
For catechumens & inquirers
If you have started wondering what becoming Orthodox would actually involve: the questions people ask, and who to ask them.
The Divine Liturgy
Understand the worship of the Church, part by part.
Prayer
Orthodox prayer, and how someone begins a prayer life.
Icons
Why sacred images are part of Orthodox worship, and how to read a church.
The saints
Why Orthodox Christians honour the saints and ask for their prayers. A Cloud of Witnesses is a free resource made by members of this parish.
The Theotokos
Why Orthodox Christians honour Mary as the Mother of God — and the feast this parish is named for, kept on 8 September.
Fasting
Why fasting is part of Orthodox Christian life. How it is kept is worked out with a priest, not from an article — so treat this as a beginning.
The church year
How feasts and fasts shape the rhythm of Orthodox life. The Online Chapel gives each day's saints and readings.
Becoming Orthodox
For someone beginning to enquire seriously about entering the Church. Speak with Fr. John — no commitment is implied, and inquirers take as long as they need.
Our Faith, on this site
The parish's own introduction: worship, the sacraments, the teachings of the Church, and where to read further.
What to expect when you visit
The Archdiocese's own guide for someone walking into an Orthodox church for the first time.
